name: ford_289_gt40_180
label: Ford 289 V8, GT40 Mk I race engine, 180° "bundle of snakes" headers
notes: Sourced: bore, stroke, 10.0:1 compression (competition engine), firing order 1-5-4-2-6-3-7-8, cross-plane crank, two valves per cylinder, four twin-choke Weber 48 IDA carburettors (one barrel per cylinder, entered as individual throttles), 380 bhp at 6500 rpm and 330 lb-ft at 5500 rpm. Cylinder numbering (1-4 front to rear on the right bank, 5-8 on the left): Wikipedia's Firing order article says Ford numbers each bank in sequence, with cylinder 1 on the right bank flagged citation-needed there; Street Muscle's Ford V8 article independently calls cylinders 1 and 2 right-bank cylinders in Ford numbering. Taken from the production 289, not confirmed for the race engine: valve diameters (all production 289 heads), 11.7 mm lift and 310 degrees advertised duration (K-code High Performance cam), 41.3 mm primary diameter (a replica 180-degree header, forum source). Estimated, not sourced: rod length, where the cam lobes sit (symmetrical timing assumed), intake tract length and diameter, primary length, collector and outlet pipe sizes (open, unsilenced), rev limit, idle speed. Left to the simulator's defaults: collector volume, flywheel inertia. Headers: sourced that two pipes from each bank cross over into each of two 4-into-1 collectors so that each collector is fed every 180 degrees. Which cylinder goes to which collector is DERIVED from the firing order, not read from a drawing: cylinders 1, 4, 6, 7 into one collector and 5, 2, 3, 8 into the other, the only split of this firing order that feeds each collector evenly. The split depends only on each bank being numbered in sequence (1-4 one bank, 5-8 the other), not on which side cylinder 1 is. Same engine as ford_289_gt40 otherwise; primaries are assumed longer because they cross the engine. Also estimates: friction_scale, heat_q, burn_scale (the simulator's friction, heat-release and burn-rate scales), set with the other estimated fields so that simulated torque and power come near the published figures; no sourced number was changed.

vehicle.name: Ford GT40 Mk I (1965)
vehicle.notes: ZF DS25 five-speed transaxle. Gear ratios from Motor Sport's 1966 test of a GT40 it called identical to the Group 4 racers; final drive 3.33 is one of the two offered (4.22 or 3.33), chosen by us because only it fits the published in-gear maxima (204 mph in 5th). Weight 2,000 lb from the period spec, dry or wet not stated (2,440 lb at scrutineering per another source). Top speed is the period estimate of 190 mph on the Mulsanne. Estimated: rolling radius of the 7.00-15 cross-ply, taking the section height as 85% of its width, then 98% for deflection.
